summary: This Docker stage sets up a Docusaurus documentation site from scratch. It installs Docusaurus, copies the project files, installs dependencies, and builds the final static HTML output that will be served.

explanations.1: This starts a new Docker build stage named 'building_production' based on the 'base' image defined earlier in the Dockerfile.
explanations.4: The backslash at the end of line 4 allows the RUN command to continue on the next line, making long commands more readable.
explanations.7: After Docusaurus is installed, we change ownership of the files from root (the default) to the 'node' user so the node user can work with them safely.
explanations.13: We copy just the package.json and yarn.lock files first (before copying all source code) because Docker caches layers—if source code hasn't changed, we can skip reinstalling dependencies.
explanations.16: The '--immutable' flag tells yarn to use exact versions from yarn.lock, preventing different versions from being installed on different builds.
